rationale.summary: A mailbox storage warning from a domain whose DMARC failed, with replies directed to a different domain than the sender address.
reasoning_steps: DMARC authentication failed (high severity) indicating the message may not be from the legitimate domain owner, even though SPF and DKIM passed individually

Reply-to domain 'campus-it-help.example' differs from sender domain 'campus-it-notices.example' (medium severity), which is unusual for legitimate IT support and can redirect responses to attacker infrastructure
The message creates urgency by claiming 98% mailbox capacity and imposing a Friday deadline, a common social engineering tactic
The link domain matches the sender domain (campus-it-notices.example), which is mildly consistent but does not offset the authentication failures
Low hop count (2) and recent origin IP may indicate direct sending rather than routing through legitimate organizational mail infrastructure
rationale.recommended_action: Escalate for domain verification. Check whether 'campus-it-notices.example' and 'campus-it-help.example' are legitimately owned by the organization. Contact IT via known-good channels to confirm whether this storage warning campaign is genuine. Do not click the link or reply until domains are validated.
